questions.prompt: What was the first U.S. capital under the Constitution?
questions.fact: It served as capital from 1789, and Washington was inaugurated there before the seat of government moved on to Philadelphia and finally to Washington.

questions.prompt: Which acid is naturally found in the human stomach?
questions.fact: Stomach acid is strong enough to dissolve metal. The stomach survives it by replacing its own lining every few days.

questions.prompt: In tennis, what is it called when a player serves two faults in a row?
questions.fact: A double fault hands the point straight to the opponent, which is why second serves are almost always slower and safer.

questions.prompt: What town do The Simpsons live in?
questions.fact: The town was named for one of the most common place names in America, and the state is deliberately never confirmed.

questions.prompt: What is the capital of Denmark?
questions.fact: More people commute by bicycle than by car in the city centre, on a network built deliberately over decades.

questions.prompt: Who carries the Ring for much of 'The Lord of the Rings'?
questions.fact: He carries the Ring but does not destroy it. At the very last moment he claims it for himself, and Gollum ends the quest by accident.

questions.prompt: What does a browser cache store?
questions.fact: The cache keeps copies so a repeat visit loads faster, which is also why a page can look out of date until you force a refresh.
